mainTopic: A husband's double status as יורש and לוקח, and then the new chapter's rule on dividing a large or small estate between sons and daughters.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about whether a husband who inherits his wife counts as a יורש (heir) or a לוקח (buyer). A source about יובל suggests he is an heir. רבא objects with a תקנה from אושא that lets the husband take back his wife's sold נכסי מלוג from the buyers, which treats him like a buyer. רב אשי answers that the רבנן gave him both statuses and apply whichever one prevents a loss. The buyers' loss in the אושא case does not count, because they knowingly bought from a married woman. The chapter יש נוחלין then ends, and a new משנה rules that in a large estate the sons inherit and the daughters are supported, while in a small estate the daughters are supported and the sons go begging. אדמון protests, and רבן גמליאל agrees with him. The גמרא defines a 'large' estate: רב says enough for twelve months, but שמואל and רבי יוחנן say enough to support everyone until the daughters become בוגרות. The amud ends as the גמרא starts asking about an estate that falls short of that measure. The question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof from יובל: a husband who inherits his wife keeps the land
steps.stepSummary: The last words of a quoted source: 'one who inherits his wife' is in the list of people whose land does not go back in the יובל year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote, begun before this section, from a list of people whose land does NOT return to its original owner in יובל. This last item supports the idea that a husband inherits his wife as a יורש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A buyer has to give land back in יובל, but an heir keeps it. Since a husband who inherits his wife keeps her land in יובל, he must count as a יורש and not a לוקח. That backs up רבין's ruling, which assumes the husband is an heir.

keyTerms.meaning: A husband who inherits his wife's property after she dies
The Jubilee year, when sold fields go back to their original owners
An heir

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new statement. It is the tail end of a quote that started before this section, so the proof is really the whole list it ends.

phrases.english: And one who inherits his wife!
phrases.notes: This finishes a list of people whose land does not go back in יובל, so this husband keeps his wife's land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a proof begun before this section, supporting רבין's ruling that the husband is a יורש.
steps.raayaObject: That a husband who inherits his wife has the status of a יורש
steps.raayaSupportSource: The list of people whose land does not return in יובל, which includes היורש את אשתו

steps.title: רבא objects: the אושא ruling treats the husband as a buyer
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether we can really be sure the husband is a יורש. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא reports a תקנה from אושא that treats the husband like a לוקח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Now that רבין sent his letter, do we really know the husband is an heir? רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: In אושא they made a rule that if a woman sold her נכסי מלוג while her husband was alive, and then she died, the husband takes the property back from the buyers.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges the idea that a husband is simply a יורש. He brings the אושא rule, which treats the husband like a לוקח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An heir cannot take back something the deceased already sold, because it was gone before he inherited. A buyer, though, can take back land from someone who bought it from the seller later. Since the husband takes the field back from the buyers, the אושא rule treats him like an earlier buyer, which clashes with the proof from יובל.

keyTerms.meaning: The town where the רבנן made important rules (תקנות)
They made a rabbinic rule
The wife's own property; the husband only gets the produce or income from it
Buyers
Takes away from someone's possession

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
And now that he sent it, do we really know?!
phrases.notes: He means רבין, who sent the letter saying the husband counts as an heir.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina say:
In Usha they instituted:
a woman who sold her melog property
during her husband's lifetime, and then died —
the husband takes it back from the buyers.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: וְהַשְׁתָּא דִּשְׁלַח, מִי יָדְעִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 1 that the husband is clearly a יורש.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption, from רבין's letter and the יובל source, that a husband inherits his wife as a יורש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The אושא rule lets the husband take sold property back from buyers, which only a לוקח can do. So the husband looks like a buyer, not an heir.

steps.title: רב אשי: the husband gets whichever status is better for him
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the רבנן gave the husband both statuses, יורש and לוקח, and apply whichever one protects someone from a loss in each case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: The רבנן made the husband like an heir, and they also made him like a buyer, and they apply whichever is good for him. For יובל, they treated him as an heir, so he would not lose. In רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's case, they treated him as a buyer, so he would not lose. In רבין's case, they treated him as an heir so the widow would not lose.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי settles the clash. The husband is not just one thing; the רבנן gave him both statuses and pick the one that avoids a loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In יובל, being an heir lets him keep the land, so he is an heir there. In the אושא case, being a buyer lets him take the field back, so he is a buyer there. In רבין's case, being an heir protects the widow, because it obligates him to feed her.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן made him like / treated him as
A buyer
What is good for him
A loss
A widow

steps.whatToRemember: The husband has a double status, יורש and לוקח. The רבנן apply whichever one prevents a loss in that case.
steps.confusionAlert: In רבין's case the reason is NOT the husband's own good. Being treated as an heir there actually costs him, because he has to feed the widow. The reason is to protect her, and this is exactly what step 4 will notice.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key idea: the husband's status as heir or buyer is a flexible rabbinic arrangement, not one fixed category.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
A husband — the Sages made him like an heir,
and the Sages made him like a buyer,
and wherever it is good for him, they did that for him;
regarding Yovel — the Sages made him like an heir,
because of his own loss.
phrases.notes: As a buyer he would have to give the land back in יובל; as an heir he keeps it.

phrases.english: Regarding the case of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina —

phrases.aramaic: שַׁוְּיוּהוּ רַבָּנַן כְּלוֹקֵחַ, מִשּׁוּם פְּסֵידָא דִידֵיהּ.
phrases.english: the Sages made him like a buyer, because of his own loss.
Regarding Ravin's case — because of the widow's loss,
phrases.notes: This is his father-in-law's widow, who gets fed from the property.

phrases.english: the Sages made him like an heir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves רבא's challenge in step 2 by showing that both sources can be right.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing: the husband has a double status, applied case by case to prevent a loss
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the husband must be either always a יורש or always a לוקח, so the יובל source and the אושא rule contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן gave him both statuses and apply whichever one prevents a loss: heir for יובל, buyer for אושא, heir for רבין's widow.

steps.title: Challenge: in the אושא case the buyers lose out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אשי: in רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's case the buyers take a loss, yet the רבנן still made the husband a buyer.
steps.simpleTranslation: But in the case of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, the buyers take a loss, and still the רבנן made him like a buyer!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes a hole in רב אשי's answer. If the רבנן care about other people's losses, as they did for the widow, why ignore the buyers' loss in the אושא case?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבין's case, the widow's loss outweighed the husband's own interest. In the אושא case, the buyers lose their purchase, but the רבנן still sided with the husband. So the rule 'avoid a loss' seems inconsistent: whose loss counts?

keyTerms.meaning: But look — opens a challenge
There is

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא גַּבֵּי דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא,
phrases.english: But regarding the case of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina,
where there is a loss to the buyers,
and still the Sages made him like a buyer!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא גַּבֵּי דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא, דְּאִיכָּא פְּסֵידָא לְלָקוֹחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב אשי's answer from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's rule that the רבנן choose the husband's status to prevent a loss, including someone else's loss, as with the widow
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If someone else's loss, like the widow's, can override the husband's interest, then the buyers' loss in the אושא case should also count. Yet there the רבנן made him a buyer, against the buyers.

steps.title: The buyers brought the loss on themselves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the buyers in the אושא case caused their own loss. They should never have bought property from a married woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, they caused their own loss. Since there is a husband, they should not have bought from a woman who lives under a husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אשי by explaining that the buyers' loss does not count, because they caused it themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי said the רבנן choose the status that keeps people from losing out. The challenge was that the buyers lose out when the husband is treated as a לוקח. The answer is that the רבנן only protect people who did nothing wrong. Someone who knowingly buys from a married woman took that risk on himself.

keyTerms.meaning: They caused a loss to themselves
To buy
Under a husband (married, under his authority)

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי's rule stands. The husband is both a יורש and a לוקח, and the רבנן use whichever status protects people. But they do not protect someone who caused his own loss.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets an important limit: a תקנה meant to prevent loss does not shield someone who walked into the loss with open eyes.

phrases.english: There, they caused the loss to themselves –
phrases.notes: 'There' means the אושא case from step 2, where people bought property from a married woman.

phrases.english: since there is a husband,
they should not have bought
from a woman who sits under a husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 4 against רב אשי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: a loss someone caused himself is not the kind of loss the רבנן protect against.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The buyers' loss seemed to show that the רבנן did not care about preventing loss.
steps.terutzMaskana: The buyers knew there was a husband and took the risk, so the rule of preventing loss does not apply to them.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק יש נוחלין
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the chapter יש נוחלין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, יש נוחלין.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the chapter יש נוחלין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is argued here. It is the traditional farewell to a finished chapter.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said when finishing a chapter)

phrases.english: We will return to you, יש נוחלין

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the last sugya ends.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter יש נוחלין is complete.

steps.title: Large estate versus small estate: sons and daughters
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that in a large estate the sons inherit and the daughters are supported. In a small estate the daughters are supported and the sons must go collecting.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man dies and leaves sons and daughters: when the property is large, the sons inherit and the daughters are supported. When the property is small, the daughters are supported, and the sons ask for charity at the doors.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter opens with a משנה about how a father's estate is divided between his sons and his daughters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sons are the legal heirs, but daughters have a right to be supported from the estate until they grow up. When there is plenty, both rights can be met. When there is not enough, the daughters' support comes first, even though that leaves the sons with nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: A large estate
A small estate
They will be supported (fed and provided for)
They will ask at the doors (go begging for charity)

steps.confusionAlert: In a small estate the daughters do not 'inherit.' They only get support. But in practice that support takes everything, so the sons end up with nothing.

phrases.english: One who died and left sons and daughters;
when the property is large –
the sons inherit, and the daughters are supported.
A small estate –
the daughters are supported,
and the sons ask at the doors.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter, so there is no link to the previous sugya.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Large estate: sons inherit, daughters are supported. Small estate: daughters are supported, sons get nothing.

steps.title: אדמון protests, and רבן גמליאל agrees
steps.stepSummary: אדמון objects that a son should not lose out just because he is male. רבן גמליאל sides with אדמון.
steps.simpleTranslation: אדמון says: Just because I am male, I lose out? רבן גמליאל said: I agree with the words of אדמון.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a disagreeing opinion: אדמון objects to the small-estate rule, and רבן גמליאל agrees with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אדמון speaks as if he were one of the sons. It makes no sense to him that being the heir should leave him worse off than his sisters. He holds that the sons should also get support from a small estate, and רבן גמליאל approves of this view.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא, one of the judges of ירושלים
I lost out
I agree with the words of

phrases.aramaic: אַדְמוֹן אוֹמֵר: בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁאֲנִי זָכָר, הִפְסַדְתִּי?!
phrases.english: אדמון says: Because I am male, I lost out?!
phrases.notes: He speaks as if he were one of the sons. It is a protest, not a real question.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: רוֹאֶה אֲנִי אֶת דִּבְרֵי אַדְמוֹן.
phrases.english: רבן גמליאל said: I see the words of אדמון as correct.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְמוֹן אוֹמֵר: בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁאֲנִי זָכָר, הִפְסַדְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissenting view against the small-estate ruling of the first opinion in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אדמון, supported by רבן גמליאל, holds that sons should not be left with nothing in a small estate.

steps.title: How big is a 'large' estate?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how much property counts as a large estate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for a definition of the משנה's word 'large.' This question sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole rule in the משנה depends on whether the estate is large or small, but the משנה never says where the line falls. The גמרא needs that line to know when the sons inherit.

keyTerms.meaning: And how much?

phrases.english: גמרא: And how much is 'large'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of a key term in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The amount of property that makes an estate 'large.'

steps.title: רב: enough to feed everyone for twelve months
steps.stepSummary: רב defines a large estate as one that can support both the sons and the daughters for twelve months.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Enough that both these and those can be supported from it for twelve months.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the first answer: a large estate is one that can feed all the children for a year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'These and those' means the sons and the daughters together. If the estate can support all of them for twelve months, it counts as large, and the sons inherit it.

keyTerms.meaning: These and those (the sons and the daughters)
Twelve months

phrases.english: רב יהודה said that רב said:
Enough that these and those can be supported from it
for twelve months.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A large estate is enough to support the sons and the daughters for twelve months.

steps.title: שמואל: that is a minority view; the חכמים say until the daughters grow up
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says רב's measure belongs to רבן גמליאל בר רבי, but the חכמים require enough to support everyone until the daughters become בוגרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I said this before שמואל, he said: This is the view of רבן גמליאל בר רבי. But the חכמים say: Enough that both these and those can be supported from it until the daughters reach maturity.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה reports that שמואל pushed back. שמואל said רב's twelve-month measure is only one opinion, and the main view of the חכמים is stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל does not deny that someone held the twelve-month view. He says it belongs to רבן גמליאל בר רבי alone. The חכמים set a much bigger requirement: the estate must cover everyone until the daughters become בוגרות, which can take far longer than a year.

keyTerms.meaning: Before him (in front of him)
רבן גמליאל, son of רבי יהודה הנשיא
That they become בוגרות (reach full maturity)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up this רבן גמליאל בר רבי with the רבן גמליאל in the משנה who agreed with אדמון. They are two different people.

phrases.english: When I said it before שמואל, he said:
phrases.notes: 'I' is רב יהודה, telling over what happened when he repeated רב's answer.

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בַּר רַבִּי,
phrases.english: This is the statement of רבן גמליאל בר רבי,
but the חכמים say:
Enough that these and those can be supported from it
until they reach maturity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Treats רב's answer as a minority opinion and gives the view of the חכמים instead.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, a large estate must support the sons and daughters until the daughters become בוגרות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the main measure for a large estate, which decides whether the sons inherit or the daughters' support comes first.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן agrees with שמואל's measure
steps.stepSummary: A statement of רבי יוחנן is brought. It says a large estate is one that can support sons and daughters until the daughters become בוגרות, which matches what שמואל said in the name of the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught in another place. When רבין came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן (some say רבה בר בר חנה said it in the name of רבי יוחנן): any estate that can support both the sons and the daughters until the daughters become adults counts as large. If it is less than that, it counts as small.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up שמואל by showing that רבי יוחנן, a great אמורא in ארץ ישראל, gave the same measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב had said twelve months. שמואל said that is only the view of רבן גמליאל בר רבי, and the חכמים measure until the daughters become בוגרות. רבי יוחנן's statement uses that same measure, so שמואל's report about the חכמים is supported.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was also stated': brings another אמורא who says the same thing, as support
'When רבין came': רבין brought teachings from ארץ ישראל to בבל
'And some say': a second version of who said the statement
'These and those': here, the sons and the daughters
Large / small: the two kinds of estate in the משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the standard definition of a 'large estate' as running until the daughters become בוגרות, not just twelve months.

phrases.english: It was also stated:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: When רבין came, he said that רבי יוחנן said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: and some say that רבה בר בר חנה said that רבי יוחנן said:
Any property from which both these and those can be supported
phrases.notes: 'These and those' means the sons and the daughters.

phrases.english: until the daughters become adults is a large estate;
if it is less than this, it is a small estate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports שמואל's statement in Step 11 against רב's twelve-month measure in Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's claim that the חכמים measure a large estate until the daughters become בוגרות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A teaching of רבי יוחנן, reported by רבין or by רבה בר בר חנה.

steps.title: What if the estate cannot last until the daughters are adults
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins asking about an estate that cannot support both sons and daughters until the daughters become בוגרות. The question continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if there is not enough to support both the sons and the daughters until the daughters become adults...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new question about an estate that falls short of the 'large' measure. The rest of the question comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now know what counts as large. The גמרא turns to the case where the estate is not that big, and starts to ask how the money is divided then. The full question has not yet been stated here.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if there is not': opens a case where something is missing
Until they become adults (בוגרות): the point where the daughters' support ends

phrases.english: And if there is not enough for these and those
until the daughters become adults,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לֵיכָּא לְאֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ עַד שֶׁיִּבְגְּרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the definition in Step 12 by asking about an estate smaller than that measure.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What happens when the estate cannot support both sons and daughters until the daughters become בוגרות (the question finishes on the next amud).
